chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Nafi', who said:

We sought permission to enter upon Abu 'Abd Allah (عليه السلام), and sent word to him, so he sent word back to us: 'Enter two by two.' So I entered, along with a man who was with me, and I said to the man, 'I would like you to ask permission regarding the question.' He said, 'Yes.'

So he said to him, 'May I be made your ransom, my father was among those whom Banu Umayyah took captive. I have known that Banu Umayyah had no right to forbid or permit, and that they possessed no right, whether little or much, in what was in their hands; rather, that belonged to you. So when I remember the condition in which I was, there enters into me from that something that nearly corrupts my mind in my present state.' So he said to him, 'You are absolved with respect to whatever there was of that, and everyone after me who is in a condition like yours is absolved from that.'

He said: Then we stood up and went out, and Mu'attib preceded us to the group who were sitting and waiting for the permission of Abu 'Abd Allah (عليه السلام). He said to them, ''Abd al-'Aziz ibn Nafi' has attained something the like of which no one has ever attained at all.' It was said to him, 'What is that?' So he explained it to them.

Then two men stood and entered upon Abu 'Abd Allah (عليه السلام), and one of them said, 'May I be made your ransom, my father was among the captives of Banu Umayyah, and I have known that Banu Umayyah had no right in any of that, whether little or much, and I would like you to make me absolved from that.' He said, 'And is that for us? That is not for us. We have no right to permit nor to forbid.'

So the two men went out, and Abu 'Abd Allah (عليه السلام) became angry. Then no one entered upon him that night except that Abu 'Abd Allah (عليه السلام) began by saying to him, 'Do you not wonder at so-and-so? He comes to me seeking from me legalization regarding what Banu Umayyah did, as though he thinks that belongs to us.' And no one benefited that night, whether by little or much, except the first two, for they had been sufficed regarding their need.

key_terms.بَنُو أُمَيَّةَ: the Umayyad ruling clan referenced as having wrongfully taken captives and property
key_terms.سَبَايَا: captives taken in war or seizure
key_terms.فِي حِلٍّ: being absolved or released from liability in the matter mentioned

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith from al-Kafi say about absolution regarding matters connected to Banu Umayyah and the authority to make things halal or haram?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an incident in which Imam Abu 'Abd Allah (عليه السلام) responded to a man distressed over property and status connected to Umayyad captivity. The Imam (عليه السلام) granted personal absolution in one case, but rejected the notion that the Ahl al-Bayt (عليهم السلام) independently declare things halal or haram, highlighting both the oppression of Banu Umayyah and the limits of religious authority as expressed in the exchange.
